predecessors.name: Greek city-states (independent poleis)
predecessors.text: the island, where Lindos, Ialysos and Kameiros 'united to form one territory' in 408 BC and built a new capital at its northern end

successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: the island, nominally independent after the alliance of 164 and sacked by Cassius in 43

ledger.x: 408 BC: the cities of Rhodes unite.
188: Rome's settlement at Apamea gives Rhodes Caria and Lycia.
188 (disputed): the part of Caria and Lycia outside the incorporated Peraia is tributary to Rhodes.
167 (disputed): the tributary remainder is lost with the rest.
167: Rhodes submits to Rome and loses the wider Peraia.
39 BC: the last Asian domains go.
39 BC (bridge): the Rhodian state leaves the map.

wars.name: Roman-Seleucid War
wars.outcome: Rhodes fought alongside Rome and, by the Treaty of Apamea of 188, 'was rewarded with territory and enhanced status'; most of Lycia and Caria became the Rhodian Peraia.

wars.name: Third Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Rhodes sent envoys to Rome in about 169 wanting peace and citing its friendship with Perseus; the message 'was considered arrogant' and Rome's good graces for Rhodes ended.

certainty.note: No frontier is given for the Peraia on any page; the island is sharp by coast.
